title: Open Files & Rooks
subtitle: Rooks belong on open files — and then on the 7th rank.
goals: Seize open files before your opponent
Double rooks for an unstoppable invasion
Feast on the seventh rank — carefully

steps.say: Rooks are your least mobile pieces at the start and your most powerful in the endgame — IF you give them what they crave: open files. A file with no pawns on it is a highway into the enemy position. Strategy rule one: put rooks on open files before your opponent does.

steps.prompt: Exactly one file on this board has no pawns at all. Claim it!
hints: Scan each file for pawns — yours AND theirs. Only one is completely clear.
The d-file: not a single pawn from either side. Your rook belongs there.

line.say: The open file is yours! From d1 the rook sees all the way into Black's camp — and Black's rook is a move too late to contest it.

rejections.say: The b-file is closed — your own b2 pawn stares back at you. Rooks on closed files are spectators.
Half the e-file is dead: your own e4 pawn blocks it. The fully OPEN file was one step further.

steps.wrongSay: Find the file with zero pawns and put your rook on it.
steps.successSay: Whoever controls the only open file usually controls the endgame.

steps.prompt: One rook holds the d-file. Double up — make the invasion unstoppable!
hints: A single rook on a file can be challenged and traded. Two rooks OWN it.
Bring the a1 rook to d1, behind its partner.

line.say: Doubled! Now if Black ever contests the file, you trade once and STILL control it. The d7 and d8 invasion squares cannot be held forever against two rooks.

rejections.say: The lone raider — but ...Rd8 challenges, and after the trade your invasion is gone. Double FIRST; then when you land on d7, no one can ask you to leave.

steps.wrongSay: The file is won by weight of numbers — get the second rook behind the first.
steps.successSay: File control, then doubling, then invasion — the rook's three-act play.

steps.prompt: The d-file is yours alone. Cash it in — invade the rank where all the pawns live!
hints: The seventh rank is the classic invasion target: enemy pawns on both sides, the king cut off behind.
Rd7 — safe, dominant, attacking in two directions at once.

line.say: The seventh rank! From d7 the rook eyes b7 and f7 simultaneously and imprisons the king on the back rank. This is what open files are FOR.

rejections.say: Rxd8 — you invaded one rank too far and traded your treasure away. The SEVENTH rank was the feast; the eighth was a trap.

steps.wrongSay: Use the open file as a road — the destination is the enemy's seventh rank.
steps.successSay: A rook on the seventh is worth about an extra pawn by itself. Masters call it 'the pig' — it eats everything.

steps.prompt: Your rook is feasting on the seventh. Two pawns look edible — one bites back. Choose!
hints: Before grabbing on the seventh, check each pawn's defender.
The f7 pawn has a royal bodyguard. The b7 pawn is home alone.

line.say: Clean! The b7 pawn had no defender — and your rook STAYS on the glorious seventh rank while material ticks in your favor.

rejections.say: Kxf7! The king was guarding his own doorstep. Even on the seventh rank, count the defenders before you dine.

steps.wrongSay: One pawn on the seventh is genuinely free — the other is king-guarded.
steps.successSay: Open file → doubled → seventh rank → material. That's the complete rook strategy pipeline.
